 th Order No.06/Dated: 14 May, 2024  IA No. 10360 of 2023 in Cr. A.(DB ) No. 1956 of 2023

The present interlocutory application has been filed to release the appellant no.2 Kaushal Rani on bail, during pendency of this appeal, which has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 30.09.2023 and sentence dated 05.10.2023 passed by the learned AJC-XVIII cum Spl. Judge C.B.I.,Ranchi, in Session Trial No. 554/2017 arising out of Case No. R.C. 09(S)/2015-SC-I,vide FIR No. Kotwali (Hindpiri) P.S. case no. 742/2014(Re-registered FIR No. RC SI2015 S0009) whereby and where under appellant no.2 namely Kaushal Rani has been convicted under Section 120-B of the Indian Penal Code r/w section 376(2)(n) and sentenced to R.I. of 10 years and fine of Rs.
50,000/- and on default of payment of fine S.I. of six months, under sections 298 IPC R.I. for 6 months, under section 323 IPC R.I for 6 months, under section 506 of IPC R.I. for 2 years.
The sentences of imprisonment were ordered to run concurrently and period already undergone during the trial and investigation if any shall be set off.
IA No. 1463 of 2024 in Cr.A. (DB) No. 2045 of 2023.

The present interlocutory application has been filed to release the appellant Md. Mustaque Ahmed on bail, during pendency of this appeal which has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 30.09.2023 and sentence dated 05.10.2023 passed by the learned AJC-XVIII cum Spl. Judge C.B.I., Ranchi, in Session Trial No. 554/2017 arising out of Case No. R.C. 09(S)/2015-SC-I, vide FIR No. Kotwali (Hindpiri) P.S. case no. 742/2014( Re-registered FIR No. RC SI2015 S0009) whereby and where under appellant has been convicted under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code r/w sections 376(2)(n)/496/298/323 and 506 of IPC, additionally substantive offence under section 298 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. of 15 years and fine of Rs. 50,000/- and in default of payment of fine S.I. of six months and under sections 298 IPC R.I. for 6 months.
The sentences of imprisonment were ordered to run concurrently and period already undergone during the trial and investigation if any shall be set off.

Learned counsel for the appellants Mr. B.M. Tripathi, Sr. Advocate, submitted that at the time of alleged occurrence in the year 2014, the anti-conversion Act was not in-force and the anti-conversion, Jharkhand Freedom of Religion Act, 2017, came in-force in Jharkhand in 2017 i.e.
after 3 years of the alleged occurrence.

Leaned learned senior counsel further submitted that Section 376(2)(n) /120B of the Indian Penal Code cannot be made out against the present appellants as the Informant was married to co- convict Rakibul @ Ranjeet Singh Kohli.
It was further submitted that there is no allegation that prior to marriage, co-convict had raped the victim.
It was finally submitted that section 496 of the Indian Penal Code is bailable.

When the CBI, took up the investigation of the case, on the order of Hon'ble High Court, informant for the first time disclosed that she was married with accused Ranjeet Singh Kohli according to Hindu rites and rituals.

The learned counsel for the appellant has further submitted that appellant Md. Mustaque Ahmed was Ranjeet Singh Kohli vs The Union Of India And Another on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61600638/
2 neither named in the FIR nor in the subsequent charge- sheet submitted by the police and the learned Trial Court failed to appreciate that there was nothing in the statement given by the informant under section 164 Cr.P.C. dated 21.08.2014 which meets out any ingredients of section 120-B IPC.

sentences.text: The learned counsel further submitted that appellant Kaushal Rani is 90 years old lady.

Appellant Md. Mustaque Ahmed has lost his job and remained in custody for about 21 months and,
hence, he has been amply punished.

On the other hand, Mr. Anil Kumar, the learned ASGI, appearing for Union of India, has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellants and submitted that appellants have been convicted under sections 376(2)
(n)/496/298/323 and 506 of IPC with aid of section 120-B IPC.

Learned counsel has pointed out from the deposition of the victim PW-4 and submitted that victim in her deposition had stated that entire occurrence took place from May, 2014 to June, 2014 when Shooting Summer Camp was organized.

In the Summer Camp the appellant Md. Mustaque Ahmed used to come along with his rifle for practice and introduced himself as Registrar (Vigilance) of Ranchi High Court and,
thereafter, Md. Mustaque Ahmed had introduced her with accused Ranjeet Singh Kohli.

Victim has deposed that marriage was solemnized in Radission Blue, Ranchi, but, ceremony of Saptpadi was not performed and, hence, learned ASGI, submitted that marriage was not complete as per section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act and hence there was no marital status of husband and wife between the accused Ranjeet Singh Kohli and the victim.
But, accused Ranjeet Singh Kohli, used to rape her on gun point.
Learned ASGI further submitted that in the facts and circumstances prevalent he will not oppose the bail of appellant Kaushal Rani, as she is 90 years old lady.
Learned counsel for OP No.2 or the victim, Mr. Ajit Kumar, Sr. Advocate without opposing the age aspect of the appellant, Kaushal Rani, opposed her bail application.

But, he has in particular opposed the bail of the appellant Md. Mustaque Ahmed and submitted that this appellant being a Government Servant misused government machinery and bodyguard and spoil the life of the victim and hence, he shall not be granted privilege of bail.
He has also repeated and endorsed arguments of the learned ASGI on section 120-B IPC.

Prima facie, case under section 496 of the Indian Penal Code is made out against the appellant Md.
Mustaque Ahmed which is punishable up to the maximum period of seven years.
Appellant is in custody for about 21 months.

Accordingly, in the facts and circumstances, we are inclined to suspend the sentence awarded to the appellant No.2, namely, Kaushal Rani in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1956 of 2023 and the appellant,
namely, Md. Mustaque Ahmed in Cr. Appeal (DB) No.2045 of 2023.

Therefore, they are directed to be released on bail, during pendency of the appeals, on executing bail-bond of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned AJC-XVIII cum Spl. Judge C.B.I., Ranchi, in Session Trial No. 554/2017 arising out of Case No. R.C. 09(S)/2015-SC-I, vide FIR No. Kotwali (Hindpiri) P.S. case no. 742/2014(Re-registered FIR No. RC SI2015 S0009).
